validity.recommendation: correct Owner2 name from 'Nicor Gas' to 'Nicor-Horizon, Inc.' (or 'Nicor-Horizon Inc, a subsidiary of Nicor Inc') and verify current parent chain (Nicor Inc -> AGL Resources 2011 -> Southern Company Gas 2016)
validity.researcher_notes: Pipeline is REAL and CORRECTLY CLASSIFIED (interstate gas transmission, FERC-certificated, docket family CP00-129/130/131/132, still active with a new CP26-564-000 docket filed Aug 2026). Existence is not in doubt: four independent origins (Oil & Gas Journal 2001-11-06, Natural Gas Intel 2000-02-11, Power Engineering 2002-05-14, and FERC's own Federal Register notice 00-8461 dated 2000-04-06 reporting a filing of 2000-03-23) all describe the same 71-74-mile, 36-in, 380 MMcf/d Joliet-to-McHenry-County project. BUT all four of those same sources -- the FERC notice itself, Kinder Morgan's own 'Horizon Pipeline: Company Overview' PDF, the OGJ article and the Power Engineering article -- state the JV owner is 'Nicor-Horizon, Inc.' (a subsidiary of Nicor Inc.), NOT 'Nicor Gas.' The FERC 2000-04-06 notice is explicit: 'the two members of Horizon are Natural [NGPL] and Nicor-Horizon, Inc., a subsidiary of Nicor Inc' and separately states 'Nicor Gas, an affiliate of Nicor-Horizon, Inc.' committed as a SHIPPER (300 MDth/d) -- i.e. Nicor Gas is a customer/counterparty of the pipeline, not an owner of it. The 2000-04-23 FERC tariff notice (02-9900, filed 2002 but referencing shippers) likewise names 'Northern Illinois Gas Company, dba Nicor Gas' as a separate shipper entity. So GEM's Owner2 = 'Nicor Gas' conflates the JV member (Nicor-Horizon, Inc.) with its gas-utility affiliate/customer (Nicor Gas) -- the ownership PERCENTAGE (50/50 NGPL/Nicor-side) is right, only the entity NAME is wrong. Not flagging existence/duplicate/classification concerns; this is a caveat on an otherwise sound row. Did not find a post-2016 document naming the current holder of the Nicor-Horizon interest (Nicor Inc. was acquired by AGL Resources in 2011; AGL Resources became Southern Company Gas in 2016) -- flagging the likely chain for a follow-up search rather than asserting a percent/owner change with no direct source.

validity.recommendation: consider updating SegmentCost from the pre-construction estimate ($75M) to the final in-service cost ($80M), or keep $75M but add a note on the escalation
validity.researcher_notes: SegmentCost = $75,000,000 IS a real, sourced figure -- it matches Horizon's own 2000-03-23 FERC certificate application, which states 'Horizon estimates that the total cost of the Project will be $75,411,000, excluding AFUDC' (FERC Federal Register notice 00-8461), and Natural Gas Intel's 2000-02-11 article independently reports 'a $75 million project.' However this is the PRE-CONSTRUCTION estimate. Cost escalated during the project: Oil & Gas Journal (2001-11-06, construction start) reports 'a $79 million northern Illinois natural gas pipeline,' and Power Engineering (2002-05-14, in-service announcement) reports 'its new $80 million natural gas pipeline ... is now in service.' Three dated, independent figures across the build timeline ($75M proposal -> $79M construction-start -> $80M as-built) is a normal, well-documented escalation pattern, not a data error -- but the sheet's current $75M reflects the earliest (2000) estimate for a project that has been complete and operating since 2002. Recommend the final $80M figure (Power Engineering, at completion) as the more accurate SegmentCost for a built pipeline; staging the sourced $75M as REFS_ADDED below since that is the value currently on the sheet, and flagging this concern for reviewer judgment on which vintage to record.

Everything else on the row checks out. EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed -- an unbroken, decades-long FERC docket family (CP00-129/130/131/132 in 2000-2002; ongoing tariff/compliance filings through 2002; a brand-new CP26-564-000 'North Extension Project' joint application by NGPL and Horizon filed 2026-08-12, Federal Register 2026-08-24) shows this is a real, continuously operating interstate pipeline, not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct as gas transmission (FERC-jurisdictional NGA section 7 pipeline; not gathering/processing). DUPLICATE: checked against the roster's Joliet trio -- P0195 Guardian (ONEOK, Joliet->Wisconsin) and P0214 Midwestern (ONEOK, Portland TN->Joliet) are both independently documented ONEOK assets distinct from Horizon (NGPL/Nicor-Horizon JV, Joliet->McHenry County IL); no overlap found, not a duplicate/relabel of either. SPEC: Length (117 km), Diameter (36 in) and Capacity (380 MMcf/d) all confirmed by 3-4 independent sources each (OGJ, NGI, Power Engineering, FERC) -- see fills[] for the ref-support detail. Location (Joliet -> McHenry County, IL) confirmed by the same four sources. Status=operating confirmed current as of 2026-08 via the new FERC docket. FuelSource and Pressure could not be sourced (see fills[], UNRESOLVED) -- Joliet is a multi-pipeline supply hub, not a single named field, so FuelSource is correctly left blank rather than forced. | ORCHESTRATOR 2026-09-15: tier/independent corrected (tier, independent). cross_row_leads.facts: NOT a fix to any existing GEM row -- flagging for the orchestrator as a possible future DISCOVERY candidate. On 2026-08-12 NGPL and Horizon Pipeline Company jointly filed FERC docket CP26-564-000 ('North Extension Project'): a new ~11.5-mile pipeline lateral from Lake County, Illinois to Kenosha County, Wisconsin, plus new compressor stations (CS 119 in Lake County, a new unit at CS 312 in Livingston County, a new unit at existing CS 113 in Will County), to deliver 185,000 Dth/d incremental firm capacity to Wisconsin Electric Power Company in southern Wisconsin. Estimated cost $438,467,975. Filed, not yet approved or built (intervention deadline was 2026-09-09) -- too early to stage as a GEM row, but worth tracking since it would extend the Horizon/NGPL system into Wisconsin for the first time and is exactly the kind of project a future Illinois/Wisconsin gas sweep or Discovery run should pick up.
